review_cost.rationale: One round of small, localized changes — none structural, but the failure-caching and timer leak are things I'd want fixed before approving.

findings.issue: apiFetch caches the promise itself, so a network error or non-ok response is cached as null for the lifetime of the process: a single transient failure permanently renders that resource as a 404 / 'Not found' page.
findings.suggestion: Cache only successful results (or cache.delete(url) on rejection/non-ok) so failures are retried on the next request.

findings.issue: EvoNode is rendered unguarded while data.js:244 can return evolution: null (failed evolution-chain fetch), throwing during render with no ErrorBoundary to catch it — the whole page goes blank.
findings.suggestion: Guard with <Show when={d().evolution}> and add an ErrorBoundary per the data-fetching guide.

findings.issue: The 250 ms search debounce timer is never cleared on cleanup; if the user types then clicks a Pokémon card, the pending navigate('/?q=…') fires after unmount and yanks them back to the filtered home page.
findings.suggestion: Clear the timer in onCleanup (or track the latest input value and no-op if the route has changed).

findings.issue: All API errors are swallowed to null, so an API outage shows 'No Pokémon found' on the home page and 404 pages elsewhere — misleading failure modes with no way to distinguish 404 from 5xx.
findings.suggestion: Let unexpected errors throw and render an ErrorBoundary fallback; reserve null for genuine 404s (res.status === 404).

findings.issue: Query-string state is built by hand with URLSearchParams and navigate() in two places (updateParams and pageHref) instead of the router's useSearchParams setter.
findings.suggestion: Use the useSearchParams setter (single source of truth for filter state) and derive page hrefs from it.

findings.issue: num() is duplicated verbatim in app/src/routes/moves/[name].jsx:14.
findings.suggestion: Move the em-dash fallback for missing values into src/lib/util.js next to EM_DASH.

findings.issue: The Moves section hand-rolls the section/aria-labelledby markup that the Section component already provides (including its anchor prop), creating an inconsistent pattern in the same file.
findings.suggestion: Use <Section title="Moves" anchor="moves" ref={movesEl}> so all regions come from one component.

findings.issue: Hash scrolling is done via a one-shot onMount window.location.hash check, which won't re-scroll when the user changes the game select (navigate to ?game=…#moves on the same route).
findings.suggestion: Also scroll when location.hash changes (createEffect on the hash, or rely on the router's hash-scroll support) rather than only on mount.

summary: A well-structured, genuinely current-SolidStart app: vite.config, query/use-server data layer, preloading and not-found handling all match the v2 docs, and the single data-module boundary keeps routes thin. The blocking issue is error handling: the response cache stores failures forever and one unguarded null can crash the Pokémon page with no ErrorBoundary. Fix those plus a debounce-timer leak and this merges cleanly.
